articles.title: G4 Nations Revive Push for Text-Based Negotiations on UNSC Reform
articles.summary: India alongside G4 members re-emphasizes the urgent necessity for text-based negotiations to overhaul the UN Security Council structural composition.
prelims: G4 comprises India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan, mutually supporting permanent UNSC seats.
Text-based negotiations (TBN) refer to working on a unified draft text containing all member states' proposals.
UNSC expansion requires a two-thirds vote in the UN General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of member states, including all P5 members.
articles.mains: Critically analyze the structural impediments to UN Security Council reforms and evaluate India's strategic leverage in pressing for permanent membership.

articles.title: MeitY Releases Draft Guidelines on Ethical AI and Algorithmic Accountability
articles.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology introduces draft frameworks ensuring algorithmic transparency and bias mitigation in public service deployment.
prelims: Establishes mandatory algorithmic impact assessments for high-risk AI deployments in governance.
Complements the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act by enforcing data minimisation principles in model training.
Proposes a National AI Ethics Board under the aegis of the IndiaAI Mission.
articles.mains: Discuss how ethical AI governance balances technological innovation with fundamental constitutional rights under Article 21.

articles.title: Environment Ministry Introduces National Framework for Biodiversity Credits
articles.summary: India launches a draft framework for biodiversity credits to incentivize private sector investments in ecological restoration and habitat preservation.
prelims: Biodiversity credits are verifiable, measurable, and tradeable units representing specific positive ecological outcomes.
Aligns with Target 19 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) on mobilizing financial resources.
Unlike carbon offsets, biodiversity credits focus primarily on ecosystem restoration and non-equivalence avoidance.
articles.mains: Examine the potential and challenges of market-based mechanisms like biodiversity credits in achieving India's targets under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).

articles.title: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan Achieves Inter-Ministerial Spatial Data Integration
articles.summary: The PM Gati Shakti platform integrates over 1,400 GIS data layers across 44 central ministries to optimize multimodal infrastructure planning and reduce logistics costs.
prelims: PM Gati Shakti uses GIS-based spatial planning tools developed by BISAG-N (Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics).
Aims to reduce India's logistics costs from ~13-14% of GDP to global benchmarks of 8-9%.
Includes the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS) as the institutional monitoring body.
articles.mains: Evaluate the role of spatial data integration under PM Gati Shakti in overcoming legacy infrastructural bottlenecks and enhancing supply chain resilience.

articles.title: IMD Expands Urban Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) across Coastal Cities
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department expands high-resolution Doppler Weather Radar networks to strengthen urban flood forecasting and coastal disaster management.
prelims: Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS) integrate meteorological, hydrological, and oceanographic hazard assessments.
Operates in conjunction with C-FLOWS (Coastal Flood Warning System) and X-band radar technology.
Aligns with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030) Target G on early warning availability.
articles.mains: Detail the imperative for hyper-local early warning systems in Indian coastal metros amidst increasing climate-induced extreme precipitation events.
